source.title: OASIS: Mitigating Harmful Fine-tuning Attacks on LLMs via Orthogonal and Adaptive Safety Alignment Strategy
source.authors: Jiayu Tang; Guo-Wei Peng; Qiuhao Xie; Yu-Ning Yang; Xiu-Rui Xie; Gui-Song Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates harmful fine-tuning on safety-aligned models and measures unsafe-response rates, but uses its own FTaaS setup and Harmful Score rather than reproducing the original studies’ methods. It also tests selective layer updates as a defense.
record.gate_note: The paper reports harmful-score outcomes after fine-tuning with contaminated task data. It does not test benign-only fine-tuning, response-position KL, compliant-token prefills, suffixes, decoding changes, or training that deepens safety. Rows below record selected results under the 60-row limit; omitted results are listed in rows_left_out.
record.test_reason: This is a defense paper (OASIS). It assumes harmful fine-tuning degrades safety and reports only how its own method and rival defenses perform. No safety-aligned model's harmful score is reported before user fine-tuning, so no row shows safety being removed. The No-Align condition is a model that was never safety-aligned. The layer selection is a design choice for the defense, not a test of whether safety behaviour sits in few parameters.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that orthogonal perturbation plus adaptive selection of safety-critical layers gives a state-of-the-art safety-utility trade-off. They claim about a 60% reduction in Harmful Score against competitive baselines, with stable downstream accuracy and fewer trainable parameters. They also claim it generalizes across four LLMs and to a cross-distribution alignment/attack setting.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates defenses in a FTaaS setup: 1,000-sample downstream task fine-tuning with BeaverTails harmful contamination at p ∈ {0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4}; reports moderation-model Harmful Score. It does not reproduce the original fine-tuning or token-depth measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with contamination ratio, downstream task, defense method, and model architecture. The paper also reports an out-of-distribution alignment/attack dataset condition and hyperparameter analyses.

fits_no_version.finding: Harmful-gradient L2 norm with respect to layer activations decays with depth in Llama2-7B (Fig. 1). The authors read this as safety-sensitive modules sitting in early layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful fine-tuning gradient sensitivity concentrates in early transformer layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Under all alignment-stage defenses, Harmful Score rises steeply with the share of harmful contamination. For example, Vaccine on SST2 goes from 6.2 to 60.2 as p rises from 0.05 to 0.4.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alignment-stage defenses against harmful fine-tuning weaken as the harmful data ratio grows.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, Proceedings of the 64th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers), 2026
record.problems: The listed HS results have no uncertainty estimates stated. The paper evaluates a defined SFT-based setup and notes that its findings may not generalize to RLHF-aligned models; its evaluation is limited to textual LLMs. No benign-only fine-tuning comparison is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row limit, omitted other Table 1 methods (Booster, LISA, SafeLoRA) at each contamination ratio; Vaccine and T-Vaccine results on GSM8K and AGNews; most Table 4 results for Qwen2-7B, Gemma2-9B, and Vicuna-7B (including non-OASIS methods and p = 0.1, 0.2); and the Table 3 cross-distribution test. The six Table 4 OASIS endpoint rows were retained to show cross-model outcomes. Table 1, Table 2, Table 3, and Table 4 contain the omitted results.

untested.parts: No harmful score is reported for an aligned model before fine-tuning, so safety removal is never measured directly; only defended models are compared.
No per-token or per-position KL analysis.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
Layer selection by harmful-gradient norm serves as a defense design. It does not show that a small set of weights carries safety behaviour, for example by ablation or removal.
No token-depth deepening is trained or evaluated.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked rows to V1 and V5 and labelled them, but every row is either a defense-performance comparison or a No-Align model that was never safety-aligned. No row shows harmful fine-tuning removing safety from an aligned model, because the aligned model's harmful score before fine-tuning is never reported. The V5 link is also wrong: choosing layers for the defense is not evidence that safety behaviour is localized. Rows r47-r50 and r55-r58 duplicate r05-r08 and r13-r16. Fig. 5 shows an 'SFT' model complying after the attack, but this is a single qualitative example.

versions.untested_parts: Does not establish that refusal is removed almost entirely across models or settings; evaluates harmful-response scores after fine-tuning on task data mixed with harmful examples.
No ordinary or benign-only fine-tuning condition is reported.
No per-token KL measurement across response positions.
No compliant opening, adversarial suffix, or decoding intervention is evaluated.
Tests selective safety-alignment updates and their harmful-score outcomes, but does not identify a minimal set of weights or ranks that independently carries safety behaviour.
Does not test whether data or a training objective causes safety shallowness.
Does not train or evaluate methods intended to deepen safety beyond initial response tokens.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Llama2-7B on SST2, GSM8K, and AGNews; contaminated user fine-tuning conditions
reader_labels.reason: The reported harmful scores show unsafe responses after fine-tuning on harmful-contaminated data, with larger scores at higher contamination in many conditions (r05-r40).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: OASIS conditions and tested architectures/tasks, especially low contamination and several cross-task results
reader_labels.reason: Unsafe-response scores are often far below near-total compliance, and OASIS remains at 5.4 at p = 0.1 on SST2; results vary substantially by task, contamination, and method (r13-r16, r25-r28, r37-r46).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Llama2-7B, SST2 ablation comparing global orthogonal perturbation with adaptive layer selection
reader_labels.reason: OASIS, which selects safety-critical layers, reports lower harmful scores than Vaccine + Orth across all four contamination rates; this is evidence for utility of selective updates, not proof of a minimal safety-carrying parameter set (r51-r58).
